product: High-performance Super Series land drilling rigs plus Alpha automation/digital and EverGreen technology. Demand comes from Canadian heavy oil and Montney natural gas/condensate drilling, US oil-directed activity, and well servicing (CMP). 2026-07-28: Canada hit a record 61 rigs. Source: precisiondrilling.com.
demand: Mostly volume and mix, with modest price. 2026-07-28: Canada 61 rigs up 22%, US 35 rigs from 33; US revenue per day rose 5.4% to USD 32,802 on higher day rates and technology; Canada revenue per day fell 6% to CAD 35,448 on higher Super Single mix and fewer upfront payments. Source: precisiondrilling.com.
pricing_power: US rig reactivation costs and weak fixed-cost absorption (2026-07-28 Q2 US margin CAD 6,212 versus CAD 9,291 in Q1 2026); Middle East geopolitical cost inflation (international revenue per day fell 5%); adverse rig mix; lower Canadian upfront payments; higher depreciation; and the CRA reassessment cash call. Source: precisiondrilling.com.
competition: Not found: no low-cost manufactured substitute, since drilling is a service. For customers the substitute is cheaper lower-spec land rigs and rival contractors. Not found: evidence of a Chinese rig or service substitute relevant to Precision. Source: precisiondrilling.com Q2 release.
market_strategy: CEO Carey Ford, 2026-07-28: fourth quarter margins expected to approach USD 10,000 per utilization day; FY2026 capex of CAD 265m; reduce debt by CAD 100m in 2026 and allocate up to 50% of free cash flow to buybacks; international as an eight-rig business. Source: precisiondrilling.com and stockanalysis.com transcript.
bull: Q2 2026 revenue rose 11% to CAD 453m with Canada at a record 61 rigs and US rigs up to 43; management guides Q4 US margins near USD 10,000/day and debt fell CAD 75m by mid-year.
bear: Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA fell 10% to CAD 97m and net loss was CAD 1m; US margin CAD 6,212 missed guidance, Q3 guided CAD 7,000-8,000, plus a ~CAD 40m CRA cash call.
falsifier: Q4 2026 US margins reported near Q3's USD 7,000-8,000 per day instead of approaching USD 10,000, or US rigs fail to reach the high-40s by end-2026.
web_what_changed_30_90d: Last 90d: 2026-07-28 Q2 revenue rose 11% to CAD 453m, but Adjusted EBITDA fell 10% to CAD 97m and net loss attributable to shareholders was CAD 1m; US active rigs climbed to 43; CRA reassessment disclosed. Last 30d: 2026-09-16 NCIB renewed for up to 1,229,799 shares, about 10% of public float. Source: precisiondrilling.com.
web_true_now_not_modelled: 2026-07-28: US rig count inflecting (43 now, high-40s expected by year-end) yet reactivation costs depress Q2-Q3 margins; Q4 guided near USD 10,000 per day. New CRA reassessment implies about CAD 40m cash due late 2026 or early 2027. Higher depreciation drove a net loss. Source: precisiondrilling.com Q2 release.
web_demand_product: High-performance Super Series land drilling rigs plus Alpha automation/digital and EverGreen technology. Source: precisiondrilling.com.
web_bottleneck: Precision's own bottleneck is reactivating rigs and absorbing fixed costs while margins recover, plus the CRA tax dispute. It relieves the customer bottleneck of access to high-spec Super Triple/Single rigs and Alpha technology that improve drilling efficiency. Source: 2026-07-28 precisiondrilling.com Q2 release.
web_who_benefits_next: Second-order: automation/EverGreen suppliers, rig upgrade and certification contractors, well servicing and rental peers, and Canadian heavy-oil/Montney producers gaining market access. Middle East NOCs in Kuwait and Saudi Arabia benefit from added high-spec rigs. Source: 2026-07-28 precisiondrilling.com Q2 release and Kuwait contract.
web_who_loses: Competitors lacking high-spec rigs or technology lose share: 2026-07-28 US industry activity fell 3% while Precision US rigs rose from 33 to 35. Lower-day-rate contractors and older-rig owners are displaced. Not found: named competitor losses. Source: precisiondrilling.com Q2 release.
web_margin_collapse_risk: US rig reactivation costs and weak fixed-cost absorption (2026-07-28 Q2 US margin CAD 6,212 versus CAD 9,291 in Q1 2026); Middle East geopolitical cost inflation (international revenue per day fell 5%); adverse rig mix; lower Canadian upfront payments; higher depreciation; and the CRA reassessment cash call. Source: precisiondrilling.com.
web_low_cost_substitute: Not found: no low-cost manufactured substitute, since drilling is a service. For customers the substitute is cheaper lower-spec land rigs and rival contractors. Not found: evidence of a Chinese rig or service substitute relevant to Precision. Source: precisiondrilling.com Q2 release.
web_ceo_promised: CEO Carey Ford, 2026-07-28: fourth quarter margins expected to approach USD 10,000 per utilization day; FY2026 capex of CAD 265m; reduce debt by CAD 100m in 2026 and allocate up to 50% of free cash flow to buybacks; international as an eight-rig business. Source: precisiondrilling.com and stockanalysis.com transcript.
web_did_they_deliver: Partly. 2026-07-28: H1 2026 revenue rose 8%, Canada hit a record 61 rigs above guidance, and at mid-year debt fell CAD 75m with CAD 16m of buybacks versus CAD 100m and 50% full-year targets. But Q2 US margin of CAD 6,212 missed guidance. Q3-Q4 targets remain open. Source: precisiondrilling.com and stockanalysis.com transcript.
web_what_would_falsify: Falsifiers: the 2026-07-28 guidance that Q4 2026 US margins approach USD 10,000 per day fails if Q4 stays near Q3's USD 7,000-8,000; or US rigs do not reach the high-40s by end-2026; or further CRA reassessments exceed about CAD 40m; or Canada Q3 rigs fall below the low-70s. Source: precisiondrilling.com and stockanalysis.com.
